course_title: Young Men Against Gender Based Violence
course_description: This course is designed for young Nigerian men to explore positive masculinity and prevent gender-based violence.

lessons.title: What is GBV?
lessons.content:
Emeka is sitting at a local motor park when he hears his friends joking about beating their wives to 'keep them in line.' Emeka feels uncomfortable but stays silent.

Gender-based violence (GBV) refers to harmful acts directed at an individual based on their gender. It is rooted in gender inequality, the abuse of power, and harmful norms. GBV can be physical, sexual, emotional, or economic. Like Emeka's friends, many normalize it, but change starts when we recognize it.

lessons.title: Types and Forms of GBV
lessons.content: GBV manifests in various forms, including domestic violence, sexual harassment, rape, child marriage, female genital mutilation, and emotional abuse. It affects individuals across all social strata.

quiz.question: Which of the following is NOT a form of Gender-Based Violence?

lessons.title: Defining Masculinity
lessons.content:
Tunde lost his job last week. He feels overwhelmed, but his father tells him, 'Real men don't cry, just endure in silence.' Tunde suppresses his grief, feeling increasingly isolated.

Masculinity is a set of attributes, behaviors, and roles associated with boys and men. Positive masculinity challenges the pressure to suppress emotions. It encourages healthy expressions of manhood that reject dominance and aggression, promoting emotional honesty and respect.

lessons.title: Traits of Positive Masculinity
lessons.content: Positive masculinity includes traits like empathy, respect, responsibility, emotional intelligence, and non-violence. It promotes equality and partnership in relationships.

lessons.title: Challenging Harmful Stereotypes
lessons.content: Harmful stereotypes often pressure men to be tough, suppress emotions, and exert control. Positive masculinity challenges these norms, advocating for authenticity and respect for all genders.

quiz.question: What is a key characteristic of positive masculinity?

modules.title: The Role of Young Men in Prevention

lessons.title: Being an Ally
lessons.content:
Chukwudi is in a WhatsApp group with his classmates. A friend shares a degrading, non-consensual photo of a female classmate, and everyone is laughing. Chukwudi realizes that staying silent makes him complicit. He types a private message to his friend explaining why it is wrong and asks him to delete it.

Young men can be powerful allies in preventing GBV by speaking out against violence, supporting survivors, and promoting respectful relationships among their peers. Chukwudi chose to act as an ally rather than a bystander.

lessons.title: Promoting Equality
lessons.content: Promoting gender equality means advocating for equal rights, opportunities, and treatment for all genders. This is fundamental to preventing GBV.

quiz.question: How can young men be allies in GBV prevention?
options: B) By speaking out against violence
C) By maintaining traditional gender roles
D) By avoiding discussions about gender

lessons.title: Communication and Consent
lessons.content:
Bello has a heated argument with his partner about her decision to take a new job. His first instinct is to raise his voice and assert authority. Instead, he takes a deep breath, listens to her perspective, and respects her choice.

Healthy relationships are built on open communication, mutual respect, and enthusiastic consent. Bello's decision to communicate rather than dominate is a form of active respect. Understanding and practicing consent is crucial in all interactions.

lessons.title: Conflict Resolution without Violence
lessons.content: Disagreements are normal, but resolving conflicts without resorting to violence or aggression is a hallmark of healthy relationships. This involves active listening and compromise.

quiz.question: What is essential for building healthy relationships?
